title: MetaRefine: Score Refinement with Multi-Level Features for Image Assessment
abstract: arXiv:2610.40487v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: An image's original dimensions, aspect ratio, and composition provide important cues that can affect its technical and aesthetic quality. Image assessment methods use resizing, cropping, padding, or patch sampling to accommodate different input sizes. However, these operations can alter or obscure original geometric and compositional cues. Existing assessment models also encode rich multi-level visual evidence that can be further extracted and exploited to improve existing models. This motivates us to combine visual evidence with original-image geometry for score refinement without changing the original scoring pipelines. In this paper, we introduce MetaRefine, a metadata-aware score refinement architecture whose lightweight residual heads predict score corrections from geometry, multi-level visual features, and the frozen model's original score. translated_title: MetaRefine：基于多层次特征的图像评估分数精细化方法
translated_abstract: 图像的原始尺寸、宽高比和构图提供了重要线索，这些线索会影响图像的技术质量和美学质量。图像评估方法通常使用调整大小、裁剪、填充或图像块采样等操作来适应不同的输入尺寸。然而，这些操作可能会改变或掩盖原始的几何和构图线索。此外，现有的评估模型已经编码了丰富的多层次视觉证据，这些证据可以被进一步提取和利用，以改进现有模型。这促使我们将视觉证据与原始图像几何信息相结合，在不改变原有评分流程的情况下进行分数精细化。在本文中，我们提出了MetaRefine，这是一种元数据感知的分数精细化架构，其轻量级残差头根据几何信息、多层次视觉特征以及冻结模型的原始分数来预测分数修正。在21个数据集的100种配置实验中，MetaRefine在88种配置中提升了PLCC指标。
tldr: MetaRefine提出了一种元数据感知的分数精细化架构，利用原始图像几何信息和多层次视觉特征，通过轻量级残差头为冻结的评估模型预测分数修正，在不改变原有评分流程的前提下显著提升图像评估性能。
en_tdlr: MetaRefine is a metadata-aware score refinement architecture that employs lightweight residual heads to predict score corrections from original image geometry, multi-level visual features, and the frozen model's original score, enhancing image assessment performance without modifying existing scoring pipelines.
